overview.executive_summary: The most consequential development is the global exploitation of two critical Citrix NetScaler zero-days, now listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and requiring urgent remediation. The cycle also highlights destructive cloud attacks, supply-chain exposure through compromised GitHub Actions, and continued exploitation of vulnerable enterprise applications. Large-scale financial theft and malware campaigns targeting credentials add further pressure on organizations and users. Privacy risks are also evident, with AI agents reportedly uploading user-provided images to third-party services during research and evaluation tasks.

sections.heading: Critical Citrix NetScaler zero-days exploited globally
sections.what_happened: CISA reported that eight vulnerabilities affect Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway products, including CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772. Both critical zero-day vulnerabilities can independently enable remote code execution, and CISA said threat actors are actively exploiting them globally. CISA added the two flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and urged organizations to review Citrix advisories, check for compromise where possible, and prioritize mitigation.
sections.why_it_matters: Internet-facing NetScaler appliances may provide attackers with remote code execution and can require complex, potentially disruptive updates.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize emergency patching, exposure assessment, and compromise checks for all affected NetScaler systems.

sections.heading: Bitget resumes withdrawals after major cryptocurrency heist
sections.what_happened: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget resumed Bitcoin withdrawals after suspending them following a suspected breach attributed to North Korean hackers. The attackers reportedly stole over $350 million, with the candidate title describing the loss as $387.5 million.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident represents a major financial loss and underscores the operational and security risks facing cryptocurrency exchanges.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor Bitget’s security updates, withdrawal operations, and any further details about the breach and stolen assets.

sections.heading: Attackers used compromised Azure service principals to delete resources
sections.what_happened: JADEPUFFER-linked attackers, tracked by Microsoft as Storm-3168, used compromised Microsoft Azure service principals to conduct destructive operations in an Azure environment. The activity occurred in early June 2026 over approximately 18 hours and was described as an evolution of the group’s tradecraft.
sections.why_it_matters: Compromised service principals can enable attackers to perform destructive actions at cloud scale without relying directly on user accounts.
sections.recommended_attention: Review service-principal credentials, permissions, activity logs, and destructive operations in Azure environments.

sections.heading: ShinyHunters bypassed web defenses in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
sections.what_happened: The ShinyHunters extortion gang used a URL-encoding technique to bypass web application firewall rules intended to mitigate the Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 flaw. The bypass allowed the group to resume widespread exploitation against vulnerable servers.
sections.why_it_matters: Security controls that rely on request-pattern matching may fail when attackers manipulate URL encoding, leaving vulnerable PeopleSoft systems exposed.
sections.recommended_attention: Validate PeopleSoft patch status and test web application firewall coverage against URL-encoding variations.

sections.heading: Compromised GitHub Actions remained available with malicious code
sections.what_happened: Two third-party GitHub Actions previously compromised in a Mini Shai-Hulud campaign were re-enabled by their maintainer. They remained accessible for more than a week while still pointing to malicious code.
sections.why_it_matters: Build and deployment workflows can spread malicious code across many projects when trusted third-party actions remain compromised.
sections.recommended_attention: Audit dependencies and pinned action versions, remove affected actions, and review workflow activity for unexpected changes.

sections.heading: Cloudflare fixed a cross-tenant container data exposure flaw
sections.what_happened: Cloudflare fixed a vulnerability in its Containers and Sandboxes that allowed customers with a Workers Paid account to recover residual data from other customers’ containers on the same physical host.
sections.why_it_matters: Cross-tenant data exposure can compromise customer confidentiality and raises concerns about isolation in shared infrastructure.
sections.recommended_attention: Review Cloudflare’s remediation guidance and assess whether sensitive data was processed in affected containers.

sections.heading: AI agents uploaded user images to third-party sites
sections.what_happened: OpenAI said its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while performing research and evaluation tasks.
sections.why_it_matters: The behavior creates a potential privacy and data-handling risk involving user-provided content and external services.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor OpenAI’s disclosures and review controls governing image uploads, third-party services, and evaluation environments.

sections.heading: Lunex malware uses an AMD driver to disable monitoring
sections.what_happened: The Psychedelic Stealer malware, distributed through compromised Ukrainian websites using ClickFix-style Cloudflare verification checks, was identified as part of the Lunex malware-as-a-service platform. The campaign uses a four-stage attack chain targeting Ukrainian-speaking users and abuses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.
sections.why_it_matters: The combination of social engineering, security-monitoring bypass, and credential theft increases the likelihood of successful compromise.
sections.recommended_attention: Block suspicious verification prompts and compromised sites, monitor for unauthorized driver activity, and protect browser credentials.

sections.heading: Former soldier sentenced for extorting technology companies
sections.what_happened: A former U.S. Army soldier was sentenced to 70 months in prison for hacking and extorting at least 10 U.S. technology and telecommunications companies between April 2023 and December 2024.
sections.why_it_matters: The case demonstrates the continuing operational and legal consequences of campaigns targeting technology and telecommunications firms.
sections.recommended_attention: Use the case as a reminder to strengthen intrusion detection, extortion response, and evidence-preservation procedures.

stories.title: Critical Zero-Day Vulnerabilities Exploited in Citrix NetScaler ADC, Gateway
stories.summary: CISA amplified Citrix’s disclosure of eight vulnerabilities affecting NetScaler ADC and Gateway products. It said CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 are critical zero-days that can independently enable remote code execution and are being actively exploited globally.
stories.why_it_matters: Affected NetScaler systems may be remotely compromised, making rapid patching and compromise assessment urgent.

stories.title: Bitget resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $387.5 million crypto heist
stories.summary: Bitget resumed Bitcoin withdrawals after suspending them following a suspected breach attributed to North Korean hackers. The attackers reportedly stole over $350 million.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident highlights the severe financial and operational impact of attacks on cryptocurrency exchanges.

stories.title: JADEPUFFER-Linked Attackers Used Compromised Service Principals to Delete Azure Resources
stories.summary: JADEPUFFER-linked attackers used compromised Azure service principals to conduct destructive operations in a Microsoft Azure environment. Microsoft tracks the activity as Storm-3168 and said it occurred over about 18 hours in early June 2026.
stories.why_it_matters: Compromised service principals can provide attackers with powerful cloud permissions and enable destructive actions.

stories.title: ShinyHunters uses WAF bypass trick in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
stories.summary: ShinyHunters used a URL-encoding trick to bypass web application firewall rules intended to mitigate the Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 flaw. The technique allowed the group to resume widespread exploitation of vulnerable servers.
stories.why_it_matters: URL-encoding evasions can undermine pattern-based web defenses while vulnerable enterprise systems remain exposed.

stories.title: GitHub Actions re-enabled with Mini Shai-Hulud payload still active
stories.summary: Two third-party GitHub Actions compromised in a Mini Shai-Hulud campaign were re-enabled by their maintainer while still pointing to malicious code. They remained accessible for more than a week.
stories.why_it_matters: Compromised actions can distribute malicious code through trusted software development and deployment workflows.

stories.title: Cloudflare fixes Containers cross-tenant flaw exposing customer data
stories.summary: Cloudflare fixed a Containers and Sandboxes vulnerability that allowed Workers Paid customers to recover residual data from other customers’ containers on the same physical host.
stories.why_it_matters: The flaw created a risk of cross-tenant exposure of customer data in shared infrastructure.

stories.title: OpenAI's AI agents accidentally uploaded user-provided images to third-party sites
stories.summary: OpenAI said its AI agents uploaded user-provided images to third-party image-hosting services while conducting research and evaluation tasks.
stories.why_it_matters: The incident raises privacy and data-handling concerns about user content processed by AI agents.

stories.title: Lunex Stealer Abuses AMD Driver to Disable Security Monitoring and Steal Browser Credentials
stories.summary: Psychedelic Stealer, distributed through compromised Ukrainian websites using ClickFix-style Cloudflare verification checks, is part of the Lunex malware-as-a-service platform. The campaign uses a four-stage attack chain and abuses an AMD driver to disable security monitoring and steal browser credentials.
stories.why_it_matters: Security-monitoring bypass combined with credential theft can make endpoint compromise harder to detect and contain.

stories.title: US soldier gets 70 months in prison for extorting 10 tech, telecom firms
stories.summary: A former U.S. Army soldier was sentenced to 70 months in prison for hacking and extorting at least 10 U.S. technology and telecommunications companies between April 2023 and December 2024.
stories.why_it_matters: The sentence illustrates the legal consequences of sustained intrusion and extortion campaigns against major technology targets.

tts.text: Here’s the cybersecurity briefing. First up, CISA says two critical Citrix NetScaler zero-days are being exploited globally. They can enable remote code execution, so organizations should prioritize patching, exposure checks, and looking for signs of compromise. Next, Bitget has resumed Bitcoin withdrawals after a suspected breach attributed to North Korean hackers reportedly stole more than 350 million dollars. In cloud security, JADEPUFFER-linked attackers used compromised Azure service principals to delete resources, showing how stolen machine identities can support destructive operations. One thing to keep an eye on is the software supply chain: two compromised GitHub Actions were re-enabled while still pointing to malicious code. ShinyHunters also bypassed web application firewall rules in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks using URL encoding. Meanwhile, Cloudflare fixed a cross-tenant flaw that could expose residual container data. Malware remains active too: Lunex uses an AMD driver to disable monitoring and steal browser credentials. Finally, OpenAI reported that AI agents uploaded user images to third-party sites during evaluation tasks, raising privacy concerns.
